title: Ordinary MSET provider and retained aliases

claims.Finding: The original retail entrypoint supplies RCX=0 to the only direct caller of 12EE70; this setter is the sole direct write found to handler-table global8AEF38. The normal unchanged startup therefore installs no resource handler table.
claims.Limitations: Direct-Xref closure for the hash-pinned image, not proof against indirect stores, patches, other initializers outside recorded provenance, or an observed live value.

claims.Finding: After constructing and linking currentEntry, a null handler table branches directly to return. The constructor sets handlerIndex+1612=-1; the dispatch changes it only after the matched load callback. Ordinary null-table registration has no table load callback and retains the negative index for retirement.
claims.Limitations: Requires unchanged normal initialization and normal return; non-null custom tables and construction faults are outside this path. Does not rule out other independent callbacks.

claims.Finding: Package_ReadBase performs direct CRT _read calls and optional in-process prefix/codec work before return; it reloads nominal package+300 for all three return branches instead of reporting the read/codec result.
claims.Limitations: Normal CRT/in-process codec semantics are the explicit library boundary; helper implementations are not exhaustively audited. Nominal length cannot certify full read, decompression success or valid MSET.

claims.Finding: The ordinary reader retires overlapping registrations, calls106700, then on positive nominal result uses currentEntry in mode3 and writes the encoded entry pointer into BAR+12 and BYTE3 metadata before returning.
claims.Limitations: Limited to observed ordinary reader/mode3 provenance with known destination reservation; alternate3F99E0, nonpositive/fallback paths and third-party providers are excluded. Not a successful-content or whole-engine ownership guarantee.

claims.Finding: The resource constructor retains the supplied primary address at Entry+16 and Entry+1624, with lengths at+24/+1600. Relocation39E690 finds that exact old address plus name via12DF90 and updates both aliases before its source copy.
claims.Limitations: The aliases are not reservations or locks. Finding one update path does not enumerate callers which already hold a returned entry or primary pointer.

claims.Finding: Primary-range lookup can detach an entry when EDX is nonzero: it updates head/tail/count and Entry+8, then returns the still-live entry without clearing either primary alias or calling a destructor.
claims.Limitations: Native range arithmetic is unchecked; this lookup is not a safe bounds validator. Empty registry/head alone does not prove that retained aliases are dead.

claims.Finding: Replacement-context teardown detaches the primary registration list, destroys the RootFileData list, frees the context and clears8AEF30.12EA20 constructs/publishes a new context. These are context lifetime transitions, not proof of primary-buffer retirement.
claims.Limitations: Entry handles may outlive list membership; context identity changes must revoke admission before any metadata lookup. No global alias lifetime claim.

claims.Finding: Retirement skips the table unload callback for negative handlerIndex, unlinks the entry and calls its destructor. The destructor passes metadata+16 to conditional disk-name-table output and directly frees the entry object;12EEA0 has a separate caller callback before retirement.
claims.Limitations: The caller callback in12EEA0 is not disabled by the null handler table. Replacement-object virtual destruction and other aliases remain separate lifetime obligations; no universal no-write/no-free claim.

claims.Finding: The remaining inspected direct context users manage names or look up entries:12EB70 inserts RootFileData/dependency strings,12E980 looks them up;12DDA0/12DE20/12E230/12E310 search replacement ranges, normalized names, 16-byte digests, or replacement type/name. Their recorded bodies contain no primary-payload reload.
claims.Limitations: Returning entry aliases does not constrain downstream consumers. Context Xrefs include one explicitly excluded alternate-reader reference3F9B15; the other28 have full bodies here.

claims.Finding: The original BAR replacement-preparation switch sends Type17 to recursive BAR preparation while Type9 takes the default advance path without a specialized replacement callback.
claims.Limitations: This is the replacement-preparation dispatch only. Later Type9 construction/fixup still mutates its payload and remains covered by the separate cache/binding contract.
